governance.attested_by: SOCO-53c (lane), run 2026-09-19-soco53c-egrid-family-hr. ONE mechanism is armed against the SOCO-53 keeper: ScenarioConfig.egrid_family_heat_rates, on this lane's own re-derive of data/raw/_processed-legacy/egrid_family_heat_rates_SOCO.csv. Everything else is the keeper's recipe unchanged, measured_ct_heat_rates included. THE MECHANISM IS A rule 14 [R-ACCURATE] DATA REPAIR, NOT A TUNING CHANNEL. eGRID joins heat rate at PLANT grain (PLNT23.PLHTRT), so every generator at a multi-technology plant inherits one generation-weighted blend: Barry (3) priced 1,118.5 MW of coal + 1,821.2 MW of gas CC + 160.0 MW of gas steam all at 8.994965, and Victor J Daniel Jr (6073) priced 1,004.0 MW of coal at 8.399, which no coal boiler can physically attain (its own meter reads 12.895). The construction is each prime-mover family's own sum(UNT23.HTIAN) / sum(GEN23.GENNTAN) from the SAME eGRID vintage the plant-grain join reads -- zero free parameters, a finer read of the identical source on the identical net-annual boundary. Rule 13 [R-MEASURED]: it regenerates for a forward year from whichever vintage the join reads and responds to changed conditions; it reads no model output and no residual. Rule 25 [R-ISO-SCOPE]: SOCO's own artifact over SOCO's own plants; no other ISO's number enters, and no other ISO's artifact was re-derived. THIS LANE REPAIRED THE CONSTRUCTION BEFORE ARMING IT. The derive's own central claim -- that the family rate replaces the blend on the identical boundary -- is an IDENTITY (sum HTIAN / sum GENNTAN == PLHTRT) and is now CHECKED rather than asserted. Over SOCO's nine covered plants it partitions them with three orders of magnitude to spare: four recompose at ratio 1.000 and five at 4.05-8.40. The five are cogeneration paper mills, where eGRID steam-credits PLHTIAN and does not steam-credit the unit sheet's HTIAN, so a family rate there charges the host's process steam to the electric output. The pre-existing out_of_window guard is a per-FAMILY plausibility test and caught only the steam halves; the turbine halves landed INSIDE 3,000-30,000 Btu/kWh and were being applied -- four rows, 160.0 MW, onto CT_CHP and CC_CHP. That is rule 14's misalignment exception verbatim, so a per-PLANT boundary_mismatch flag refuses them: SOCO's artifact goes 12 applied -> 8, and the arm moves 24 rows / 6,473.2 MW at four plants only. The guard is DERIVE-SIDE, never consumer-side: a guard inside _apply_egrid_family_heat_rates is default-on and would have moved CAISO's keeper fleet from this lane (rule 25). NO src/market_sim FILE IS TOUCHED and no solve-path file moves. BOUNDARY_IDENTITY_TOL = 0.005 is a rounding allowance for a published figure and is incapable of being a tuned threshold: over all 26 covered plants in the three ISOs carrying an artifact the passing side sits at 1.0000 and the failing side starts at 2.800, so every value in (0.001, 1.8) yields the identical partition. Declared ex ante in PRECOMMIT-soco-53c-2026-09-19.md section 1.3 and never swept. RULE 19 [R-ONE-MECH], MACHINE-VERIFIED: the precedence is structural, not declared -- the family rate is applied at FRAME level in _rows_to_generators and measured_ct_heat_rates inside the ROW LOOP gated on group == 'CT_PEAKER', so the measured CAMPD loaded rate overwrites the family rate on every CT row and never the reverse. Precedence: measured CAMPD > eGRID family > eGRID plant blend. Confirmed on the built fleet: CT_PEAKER cap-weighted heat rate is BYTE-IDENTICAL (11.2666 both sides), so Greene County's computed GT family rate (14.105) and Watson's (21.925) are both entirely overwritten and nothing is priced twice. CC_CHP / CT_CHP / ST_CHP heat rates are likewise byte-identical, by the boundary guard. RULE 1 [R-STRUCT] / NO PRICE TUNING: every offer_curve_by_group band is exactly 1.0 on all 13 groups, offer_curve_overrides and offer_curve_deltas are null, and authorized_price_tuning is DECLARED NONE -- with no price benchmark for SOCO there is no residual to tune against, so the rule-1 authorized channel is UNREACHABLE in principle here, not merely unused. No band, share, floor or threshold was touched. THE EFFECT WAS PREDICTED ADVERSE-TO-NEUTRAL BEFORE THE SOLVE and is confirmed: PRECOMMIT section 2.2 registered that coal would fall, CC_REGULAR would rise with 2024 the row at risk, and that CT_PEAKER and ST_GAS would NOT materially improve -- so the two failing C1 rows would not be fixed by this arm. Delivered: COAL -0.665 / -1.855 / -1.528 TWh, CC_REGULAR +0.468 / +1.915 / +1.947, CT_PEAKER +0.234 / +0.399 / +0.157 (inside the declared 1.0 TWh falsifier). Nothing was reverted and no band was touched to move it. AUTHORIZED PRICE TUNING: NONE. SOCO has no price benchmark of any kind -- data/raw/_validation-source/actual_lmp.json carries no SOCO block and must not gain one -- so C3a / C3b / C3c are UNSCORABLE, not failed, and there is no price residual against which the rule 1 [R-STRUCT] / rule 13 [R-MEASURED] authorized offer-curve channel could be exercised. Every offer_curve_by_group band is the identity 1.0 on all 13 groups. The channel is unreachable here in principle. The governance block therefore carries NO authorized_price_tuning key by design -- the key is validated as a structured declaration whenever it is present, and declaring it here would be declaring a channel this run does not and cannot use.

disclosures.9_THE_ROOT_CAUSE_IS_COMMITMENT_PHYSICS_N: MEASURED, ZERO-LP, AND IT IS WHAT THIS LANE ACTUALLY ESTABLISHES. (a) Every offer_curve_by_group band is the identity 1.0 for SOCO, so each class is a SINGLE FLAT PRICE BLOCK — confirmed in the control's own class_band_hourly sidecar, where 2023 ST_GAS runs 1.117 / 1.138 / 1.141 / 0.600 TWh across the four bands, flat. Every curve-SHAPED lever is therefore provably inert for SOCO by construction. (b) The MEASURED cost separation between the classes is +0.713 MMBtu/MWh (CT 10.911 vs ST 10.198, CAMPD loaded hours) while the MODEL already separates them by +1.983 — 2.8x — and CT_PEAKER still over-runs by 8.221 TWh. No admissible cost-side change closes a gap the model is already overshooting. (c) The real separation is COMMITMENT: at unit grain SOCO gas boilers run 94-144 h campaigns and start ~9-11 times a year, combustion turbines run 8-9 h blocks and start ~57-60 times a year; the model gives BOTH classes min_run_hours = 0 and min_down_hours = 0, and with tranche_startup_amortization off the CT_PEAKER econ and peak tranches — which hold 10.9 of the class's 12.755 TWh in 2023 — carry ZERO startup cost. (d) The bridge that would supply it is INERT on SOCO's own data and was refused rather than solved: 68.7 % of boiler downtime gaps exceed 72 h and account for 169,303 of 171,734 gap-hours (98.6 %); only 150 unit-hours across three years fall inside the 8 h ST_GAS min-down. SOCO's boilers do not two-shift. The successor object is a commitment mechanism built for multi-week campaigns, not a gap bridge and not a pricing rule.

disclosures.10_barry_st_family_is_itself_a_fuel_blen: THIS LANE'S OWN. Barry's eGRID ST family blends its two BIT coal units with its two gas boilers, so the applied 12.610 is not either half's own rate: measured at unit grain from UNT23/GEN23, coal reads 11.699 (79.6 % of the family) and gas steam 16.159 (20.4 %). It is KEPT because it moves BOTH halves toward their own truth MONOTONICALLY, with no trade -- coal error -2.704 -> +0.911 (3.0x closer) and gas steam -7.164 -> -3.549 (2.0x closer) against the control's plant blend of 8.995. Rule 14's misalignment exception applies only where using the accurate data literally would make results LESS reflective of reality; here it makes both halves MORE so, so the exception does not apply. Daniel (6073) raises no such question: its ST family is its two SUB coal units alone, so 12.895 is a pure coal rate.
